lost-property.title: The Lost Property Office 🧸
lost-property.hook: In this town, the lost-and-found office is never empty. Whatever you leave there comes back the next morning with a note in someone else's handwriting.
lines: In this town, the lost-and-found office is never empty.
You see, every morning at 7:03, a new box appears on the counter.
Inside is whatever you lost yesterday, with a note in someone else's handwriting.
Milo was twelve, and he had lost exactly one thing: a small red toy car.
He had looked under the bed, behind the sofa, and inside his school bag.
On Tuesday, the box on the counter had his name on it.
The note said: DO NOT OPEN IT HERE.
Anya, the new girl, said her note had said the same thing.
So they carried the box outside to the empty bus stop.
Inside was the car, and a tiny paper door with a keyhole.
The car was warm. The paper door had no handle.
A shadow moved behind them. It was their own shadows, standing perfectly still.
Then the box spoke, in Milo's own handwriting: YOU'RE EARLY.
The paper door opened by itself, and the little red car drove in.
Milo looked at Anya. Her shadow was gone.
lost-property.safety: Original fictional story with children in a safe everyday setting; no violence, brands, fear tactics or sensitive topics.

shadow-runner.title: In This Town, Your Shadow Leaves First
shadow-runner.hook: In this town, your shadow clocks in before you do. Every morning at 7:03 it takes its place in line.
lines: In this town, your shadow clocks in before you do.
You see, every morning at 7:03, every shadow stands in line at the bus stop.
Milo was twelve, and his shadow had never once been early. Until Tuesday.
That morning, it walked past the school and past the bakery.
It stopped at the locked theater, holding a red ticket.
At school, the teacher asked everyone to draw what their shadow did last night.
Milo drew a straight line. Every other kid drew the same line.
Then the new girl, Anya, drew a door.
Nobody spoke. Even the shadows on the wall stayed perfectly still.
At recess, Milo followed his shadow back to the theater.
The doors opened by themselves. Empty seats faced one glowing screen.
On the screen, Milo saw tomorrow. His shadow sat in the principal's chair.
Beside it, every other shadow in town was signing something.
Milo looked down. His shadow was gone.
Then a voice from the screen said, You're early.
shadow-runner.safety: Original fictional world-rule story; no violence, brands, sensitive topics or unsafe behaviour.
